policy: Transactional SQL rejects SELECT DISTINCT, GROUP BY, built-in aggregates including windowed/nested forms, and deduplicating UNION/INTERSECT/EXCEPT. Explicit analytical backends remain valid.

selection.description: Complete tracked package Python/SQL in the authoring checkout; immutable private consumer Python and tracked SQL; fixed-seed 80-file CPython sample plus sqlite3 sources; labeled semantic controls.
selection.private_pins: Retained privately with full Python/project/lock semantic input closures; not exported.

method.diagnostic_compatibility: The qualified candidate also restores the legacy SARJ465 message anchor; unchanged findings retain existing baseline identities without changing expanded detector coverage.
method.performance_context: Observed on the shared VM; concurrent admitted workloads can affect elapsed times.
method.baseline: Original SARJ020 from the preceding public service-contract release, evaluated in the same current kernel; standalone baseline excludes new SARJ122.
method.labeled_expectations: Independent positive/negative SQL shapes, overload/function identity, EXPLAIN execution, set operation, analytical driver, suppression, namespace/dependency/re-export controls.

review.method: Independent per-file labels and complete diagnostic tuples were reconciled across three immutable before/after trials; every actual consumer finding was inspected.
review.scope: Finite supported-scope evaluation; private source, paths, identities and identifying pins remain in separate private receipts.

scope_and_limits: Python requires source-proven native transactional driver ownership; mixed backends require a proven native query receiver. Unknown dynamic sinks are not inferred.
First-party analytical contracts resolve only through the owning distribution and declared first-party dependencies; shared namespace package roots and type-only re-exports are covered.
Standalone SQL uses the existing PostgreSQL default, explicit dialect directives and established analytical database directories.
Plan-only EXPLAIN, comments, values, quoted case-sensitive user functions, scalar overloads and ALL set operations remain valid.
Existing complex-query advice is suppressed only when an unsuppressed SARJ020 error owns the same query.
No ORM or embedded TypeScript SQL ownership is claimed; a bounded consumer audit found no current transactional usage in those surfaces.
No database migration or blanket diagnostic baseline is generated. Reviewed atomic invariants require an exact reasoned exception.
